answer.generated: Transparency addresses whether a distributed system should appear to users as a single coherent system, while openness concerns whether it uses standardized protocols for interoperability. Transparency aims to minimize complexity by hiding internal distribution, allowing users to interact without understanding the underlying architecture. Openness, in contrast, prioritizes flexibility and compatibility by adopting common standards, which may sacrifice some performance for ease of integration across different systems. Both principles are essential for designing distributed systems that balance usability and maintainability.
